description: Payments of exactly 4.99 are included along with larger ones.

b.request: Include payments with an amount of 4.99 or more that link through a rental to an inventory item; group by rental and inventory store, then report each store ID with the unrounded average per-rental payment total and average payment count, ignoring missing values.
b.sql:
SELECT i.store_id, AVG(rental_totals.total_amount) AS avg_per_rental_payment_total, AVG(rental_totals.payment_count) AS avg_payment_count
FROM (
  SELECT p.rental_id, SUM(p.amount) AS total_amount, COUNT(p.payment_id) AS payment_count
  FROM payment p
  WHERE p.amount >= 4.99
    AND p.rental_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY p.rental_id
) AS rental_totals
JOIN rental r ON r.rental_id = rental_totals.rental_id
JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id
GROUP BY i.store_id;
b.raw: Include payments with an amount of 4.99 or more that link through a rental to an inventory item; group by rental and inventory store, then report each store ID with the unrounded average per-rental payment total and average payment count, ignoring missing values.

a.request: Take the payments of at least 4.99 that can be linked to a rental and, through that rental, to an inventory item (leave out payments without such a match). For each rental and store (`inventory.store_id`), total the payment amounts and count the payments. Then for each store, show the store id, the average of those per-rental totals, and the average number of payments per rental (both unrounded, ignoring missing values).
a.sql:
SELECT i.store_id, AVG(rental_totals.total_amount) AS avg_total_amount_per_rental, AVG(rental_totals.payment_count) AS avg_payments_per_rental
FROM (
  SELECT p.rental_id, i.store_id, SUM(p.amount) AS total_amount, COUNT(*) AS payment_count
  FROM payment p
  JOIN rental r ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id
  JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id
  WHERE p.amount >= 4.99
  GROUP BY p.rental_id, i.store_id
) AS rental_totals
GROUP BY i.store_id;

d.request: Include payments with amount ≥ 4.99 that link through a rental to an inventory item; for each rental and its inventory store, sum payment amounts and count payments, then report each store’s ID, the unrounded average of per-rental payment totals, and the unrounded average number of payments per rental, ignoring missing values.
d.sql:
SELECT i.store_id, AVG(rental_totals.payment_total) AS avg_payment_total_per_rental, AVG(rental_totals.payment_count) AS avg_payments_per_rental
FROM (
  SELECT p.rental_id, SUM(p.amount) AS payment_total, COUNT(p.payment_id) AS payment_count
  FROM payment p
  JOIN rental r ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id
  JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id
  WHERE p.amount >= 4.99
  GROUP BY p.rental_id
) AS rental_totals
JOIN rental r ON r.rental_id = rental_totals.rental_id
JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id
GROUP BY i.store_id;

c.request: Applying a 4.99 cutoff on the payment amount, take the qualifying payments that can be linked to a rental and, through that rental, to an inventory item (leave out payments without such a match). For each rental and store (`inventory.store_id`), total the payment amounts and count the payments. Then for each store, show the store id, the average of those per-rental totals, and the average number of payments per rental (both unrounded, ignoring missing values). Payments of exactly 4.99 are included along with larger ones.
c.sql:
WITH rental_store_totals AS (
  SELECT r.rental_id, i.store_id,
         SUM(p.amount) AS rental_total,
         COUNT(p.payment_id) AS payment_count
  FROM payment p
  JOIN rental r ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id
  JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id
  WHERE p.amount >= 4.99
  GROUP BY r.rental_id, i.store_id
)
SELECT store_id,
       AVG(rental_total) AS avg_rental_total,
       AVG(payment_count) AS avg_payments_per_rental
FROM rental_store_totals
GROUP BY store_id;
